You are working on POLUS, a Godot 4.7 first-person survival sandbox. Project root: polus (relative paths are relative to it). Browser build 'step 1' (valley map default, small 'glade' test map): chop trees with a physical axe arc, crack rocks, dig, carry, build. Server-authoritative even in solo; clients send input snapshots; the server decides and broadcasts rpc call_local events applied alike on every peer; world state deterministic (ids from counters, no global randf); fx are visual only.

THIS TASK = wave polus-feel-1: fix Maxim's playtest batch of 02.11 (18 items) on top of wave W2 (variant E: one blow law for all materials + the material test range; W2 is DONE and published as build/web-final9). READ FIRST: .orchestra/tasks/62/feel1/../feedback-0211/batch.md (his items with verbatim Russian quotes) and LOOK at the 7 screenshots in that folder with Read (01_board_close_hole, 02_board_top_edge_section, 03_board_edge_colour_seam, 04_stone_pole_thin_bridge, 05_granite_fragment_two_pieces, 06_sandstone_cracks_in_air, 07_dig_squares). Then .orchestra/tasks/62/notes.md, .orchestra/tasks/62/w2/integ/stage.md, .orchestra/tasks/62/w2/polish/stage.md, .orchestra/tasks/62/w2/main/baseline.md, and the W1/W2 part notes your files touch (.orchestra/tasks/62/w1/*/notes.md, .orchestra/tasks/62/w2/*/notes.md; APIs​ at their top). Maxim's praise to keep: «прям щас ебать кайфово рубить деревья» — do not break how chopping feels.

How the orchestrator reads his asks (use these; if the code shows a better reading, say so in your notes):
1. Point aim («в точку») is the DEFAULT aim mode of every tool; the mode toggle stays.
2. Reach (how far the hands work) = the body's own height from the floor to the head + the arm, from the eye: the player must reach the ground at his feet and around him (a fallen tree's lower branches with the small hatchet); each tool adds its own length (handle + head). Use the physique (thin / fit / god) body numbers that exist.
3. The held tool follows the body faster: sprinting or turning must never bring the tool into the camera / the face.
4. Point aim: after a strike, while the mouse has moved only a little (a small angle) since that strike, keep the strike target point and depth of that strike; a cursor that falls into the notch must not switch the hint to «близко» and stop the strikes.
5. Holding LMB = auto swing: wind up, release by itself at full wind-up, wind up again, while held. A click still works as today.
6. X-ray trajectory for every tool: the tool's strike shape (its head / blade silhouette) drawn along its path from where the swing starts to where it would end if every material on the way were air, visible through objects, plus the tool's shape drawn at the first contact. Pretty and cheap (<= ~1 ms per frame in WebGL2, few draw calls).
7-18: the bugs and asks as written in batch.md (wood: edge pass-through, colour seam at the hit, stump top cut must fall off as a piece, the wood chip in the item panel must show its real cut shape; stone: a section / infographic panel on the right like the wood section panel, a piece held by a 1-pixel bridge falls / breaks off by itself, the pick hint flickers between «скол» and «далеко», a fragment of two pieces joined by an invisible line splits (connectivity by polygons) and its texture must not swim in the panel, crack preview lines must never run through the air; range: stands vanish after running far and coming back (cylinders stay, no collision, no hits), the first load of the range hitches; ground: sharp squares when digging after the grass grew back).

TESTS (Maxim: «надо чтобы боты тестили и вообще тесты у нас чтобы такого не было»): every bug gets a headless test or bot check that FAILS before your fix (save that red log in your folder) and passes after (green log). Item 7 especially: a series of strikes from above at a board's edge at many angles, positions and tools; invariant: any swing whose swept arc crossed material either removes volume or names the reason in the log. Visual bugs (colour seam, squares, cracks in the air, panel textures) also need a numeric check where one exists (e.g. crack polyline points all inside the stone; vertex colours / UV continuity) plus a browser shot.

Numbers: wood / soil / stone / tree numbers may change ONLY where a fixed behaviour changes; write a diff per case (old vs new and why). Compare against .orchestra/tasks/62/w2/main/det_ref with .orchestra/tasks/62/w1/compare.sh (det via .orchestra/tasks/62/w1/law/det.sh); W2 battery: .orchestra/tasks/62/w2/main/regress.sh; never loosen a threshold.

Task folder: .orchestra/tasks/62/feel1/<your part>/ — notes, scripts, logs, screenshots there. RESTART SAFETY: the hub restarts and API limits kill agents; you may be a re-run. FIRST read .orchestra/tasks/62/feel1/<your part>/notes.md if it exists and continue (earlier edits are on disk). Short verified steps; after each step append to notes.md what is done, numbers, what is next. Put any API other parts need at the TOP of notes.md. Read the notes of parts that run alongside you.
Other agents may work in the same checkout at the same time. Edit ONLY the files your part owns, plus the one-line hooks your part lists (say them in notes). Re-read a shared file right before each edit. If a test fails because of someone else's half-done file, wait 1-2 minutes and retry. Run the parse check (.orchestra/tasks/55/fix/tests/parse_check.tscn, or the parse_all step of .orchestra/tasks/59/main/regress.sh) after edits.

HUB LIMITS: the whole T3 service (every agent, godot and Chrome, shared with Maxim's other projects) has 8 CPUs / 49 GiB; the hub itself is shared by ~150 users. Going over lets the OOM killer take the T3 server and every agent dies. So: in the Fix phase at most ONE godot process of yours at a time (six parts run in parallel); run 'python3 export/hub_guard.py --need-gb 3 --wait 1800 --quiet' before each godot run; prefix runs with nice -n 10; full batteries only in Integrate / Polish; the browser ONLY via export/cdp.py (project-wide lock: one Chrome at a time; it waits for the lock and for RAM), keep each browser run under ~20 minutes, never a browser and a battery at the same time; kill your servers by PID when done (never a broad pkill). Wall clock lies under load: judge perf by thread CPU (RockNode.cpu_clock / RockNode._now(), see .orchestra/tasks/62/w1/polish/notes.md 08:40).

Environment facts:
- Godot: .hub-tools/godot/godot (headless only). Web build = Compatibility renderer (WebGL2), no threads; per-instance shader parameters do NOT draw there; the web font lacks arrow glyphs (they draw as boxes); no-break spaces are ignored in the web build (step1_hud._wrap_items breaks lines itself). Physics: Jolt.
- Refresh imports ALWAYS under the lock: flock build/.build.lock .hub-tools/godot/godot --headless --path . --import.
- Headless runs: timeout 900 .hub-tools/godot/godot --headless --path . res://scenes/menu.tscn -- --solo --map=glade|valley --autotest=<bot> (bots: see .orchestra/tasks/62/w2/main/regress.sh, .orchestra/tasks/62/w1/main/regress.sh, .orchestra/tasks/59/main/regress.sh; the range bots are matbuild / materials). Headless never draws frames.
- Web build: OUT=build/web-<name> bash export/build_web.sh (serialises itself). Serve with Bash run_in_background and an explicit timeout: python3 export/serve.py <PORT> nocoi polus/build/web-<name>. Browser: python3 export/cdp.py "http://127.0.0.1:<PORT>/index.html?<query>" <outdir> --port <CDP_PORT> --size 960x540 --timeout <s> --shot MARKER=name.png ... (SwiftShader: slow; markers are console-line substrings waited for IN ORDER; KEY​:F1 actions exist; only POLUS_/CHOP_/TREE_/AUTOTEST_/ERROR lines print). The materials bot has shots modes (shots=..., POLUS_MAT_SHOT_* markers) — extend it rather than writing a new one. Look at your PNGs with Read.
- Long foreground Bash calls (builds, bots) need an explicit timeout (up to 600000 ms); longer ones go to run_in_background with timeout up to 7200000 ms.
- Perf: one action well under ~10 ms CPU where possible; per-frame aim work <= ~1 ms; nothing per frame for settled things; never read meshes back from the GPU in the web build; valley tour q=1 <= 300 draw calls / 800k primitives (the polygon stop is at 292 now: anything you add near the range must not add draw calls there).
- Snapshot bits: MECH 34-36; sharpness 37-46; aim mode 47-55; next free 56 (the Map assigns new bits).
- Player-facing TEXT in Russian, KEY NAMES in English; every new key goes into the F1 overlay world/hud/controls_overlay.gd (free keys​: L is sharpening, N, O free; T/Shift+T time skip, K, M taken).
- Never write outside the project folder (no /tmp, no $HOME). Do not commit, do not publish. Never print secrets. Match the surrounding GDScript style; smallest code that does the job.
- Your final answer is data for the orchestrator: what you did, files, every check with numbers (red before / green after for each bug), screenshot paths, open issues; be honest about anything not verified.

YOUR PART: map (folder .orchestra/tasks/62/feel1/map/). READ-ONLY on game code: you write only into .orchestra/tasks/62/feel1/map/ (notes.md and plan.md). No godot runs needed unless a quick headless probe settles a cause (then at most one at a time).
For each of the 18 items find the real cause in the code (file, function, line), the files a fix must touch, and the red-then-green test that will prove it. Then split the items into 4 to 6 PARTS that can run IN PARALLEL in one checkout:
- no file may be owned by two parts; a file several parts need gets ONE owner, the others may only add a one-line hook there that you name exactly (file + what);
- group by files, not by theme (e.g. item 13 «скол / далеко» goes with the aim / reach code if that is where it lives);
- effort 'high' only for the 1-2 parts with hard geometry / physics (e.g. item 7 edge pass-through, items 12/14/15 stone connectivity and crack paths); 'medium' for the rest;
- browser=true for parts whose items are visual (they may use the one shared Chrome via export/cdp.py);
- contracts: any API one part needs from another (names, signatures) and in what order; bits: assign snapshot bits from 56 up if any part needs them;
- risks: what could break the chop feel or the det numbers.
Write the full map to .orchestra/tasks/62/feel1/map/plan.md and return it in the schema (plan per part = what to do, in a few sentences, with the cause and the test).
